title: Ladakh votes in panchayat and municipal polls amid bitter chill after eight-year gap

ai.summary: Voters in Ladakh began casting ballots for panchayat and municipal elections after an eight-year gap since Ladakh became a Union Territory in 2019, with the first local body polls held in the high-altitude region amid freezing temperatures.

facts.claim: voters in Ladakh began casting their ballots for the much-awaited panchayat and municipal elections
facts.quote: Kargil, Nov 21: Braving biting winter temperatures across the high-altitude Himalayan desert, voters in Ladakh began casting their ballots on Saturday morning for the much-awaited panchayat and municipal elections.
Held after an eight-year hiatus, the exercise marks the first grassroots local body polls in the region since Ladakh was carved out as a separate Union Territory in August 2019.

facts.claim: the first grassroots local body polls in the region since Ladakh was carved out as a separate Union Territory in August 2019
facts.quote: the exercise marks the first grassroots local body polls in the region since Ladakh was carved out as a separate Union Territory in August 2019.

facts.claim: Polling commenced at 8:00 AM and will continue until 5:00 PM across all eight administrative districts
facts.quote: Polling commenced at 8:00 AM and will continue until 5:00 PM across all eight administrative districts—Leh, Kargil, Sham, Changthang, Drass, Nubra, Zanskar, and Sankoo.

facts.claim: To facilitate maximum voter participation in the freezing weather, the Ladakh administration declared a public holiday across the Union Territory and equipped polling stations with heating facilities alongside tight security arrangements
facts.quote: To facilitate maximum voter participation in the freezing weather, the Ladakh administration declared a public holiday across the Union Territory and equipped polling stations with heating facilities alongside tight security arrangements.

facts.claim: In urban areas, polling is underway in all 21 wards of the Leh Municipal Committee
facts.quote: In urban areas, polling is underway in all 21 wards of the Leh Municipal Committee.

facts.claim: In the Kargil Municipal Committee, voters are casting ballots for 13 out of 17 wards, as four councillors were already elected unopposed
facts.quote: In the Kargil Municipal Committee, voters are casting ballots for 13 out of 17 wards, as four councillors were already elected unopposed.

facts.claim: Out of the 192 panchayats in Ladakh, 55 sarpanches have been elected unopposed, leaving 137 seats up for grabs today
facts.quote: Out of the 192 panchayats in Ladakh, 55 sarpanches have been elected unopposed, leaving 137 seats up for grabs today.

facts.claim: Similarly, for the 1,428 panch seats, 1,186 candidates won unopposed, with elections currently taking place for the remaining 242 constituencies
facts.quote: Similarly, for the 1,428 panch seats, 1,186 candidates won unopposed, with elections currently taking place for the remaining 242 constituencies.

facts.claim: Conducting polls in late November posed steep logistical challenges, with polling parties, security personnel, and Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs) dispatched on Friday to remote, high-altitude locations—including polling booths situated as high as 15,000 feet
facts.quote: Conducting polls in late November posed steep logistical challenges, with polling parties, security personnel, and Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs) dispatched on Friday to remote, high-altitude locations—including polling booths situated as high as 15,000 feet.

facts.claim: The last municipal and panchayat elections in the region were held in September and November 2018, respectively
facts.quote: The last municipal and panchayat elections in the region were held in September and November 2018, respectively.

facts.claim: Saturday’s voting unfolds amid ongoing political discourse in the region, with the Leh Apex Body (LAB) having staged protests demanding the postponement of the upcoming Hill Council polls until 2027
facts.quote: Saturday’s voting unfolds amid ongoing political discourse in the region, with the Leh Apex Body (LAB) having staged protests demanding the postponement of the upcoming Hill Council polls until 2027.

facts.claim: Counting of votes for Saturday's panchayat and municipal elections is scheduled for December 4
facts.quote: Counting of votes for Saturday's panchayat and municipal elections is scheduled for December 4.

facts.claim: On the same day, Ladakh will also go to the polls for the 100 constituencies of its eight Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Councils (LAHDCs)
facts.quote: On the same day, Ladakh will also go to the polls for the 100 constituencies of its eight Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Councils (LAHDCs)

ai.background_note: Ladakh became a Union Territory in August 2019 after being split from Jammu and Kashmir. The Leh Apex Body (LAB) has previously protested for the postponement of Hill Council polls until 2027.
